title: Honest charts, honest reports and a one-page dashboard

say: Honest charts, honest reports, and a one-page dashboard.
This is the video for module 3 of Reporting and Performance Tracking.
A good chart lets a busy reader see your main point in a few seconds. To show change over time, use a line chart.

panel.heading: Match the chart to the message

cards.d: How a number changed over time, like monthly sales from January to June.
Which category is bigger, like sales by channel: WhatsApp, Walk-in, Instagram.
How a whole splits into parts, only with 2 to 5 slices. Never for change over time.

say: To compare categories, use a column or bar chart.

say: To show how a whole splits into parts, a pie chart works only with 2 to 5 slices.
And when your reader needs exact figures, like a funder checking each target, a simple table is best.

say: For example, Bisi's sales were 250,000 naira in January and 262,000 in February.

say: That is a real rise of 4.8%. A small, steady improvement.

say: But Sheets started her chart's axis at 240,000. So January's bar showed only 10,000, and February's showed 22,000. February looked 2.2 times taller, as if sales had more than doubled.

say: Readers judge bars by their length, so always start bar and column charts at zero. Label units and dates, and check every chart on a phone screen.

say: A manager or funder who catches one exaggerated number will doubt every number after it.

panel.heading: Ways reports mislead
items: Hiding the denominator: 30 out of how many?

say: Do not show only your best week. Do not change what you count without saying so.

panel.heading: Ways reports mislead
items: Hiding the denominator: 30 out of how many?

say: Do not count a woman twice because she attended two trainings.

panel.heading: Ways reports mislead
items: Hiding the denominator: 30 out of how many?

say: Always give the denominator. 30 women started businesses, out of 40 trained, or out of 400?

panel.heading: Ways reports mislead
items: Hiding the denominator: 30 out of how many?

say: And do not claim cause without evidence. Sales may have risen because of your flyer, or because December always brings more parties. Say it carefully: part of this is likely the festive season.

say: For example, Halima's grant target was to train 100 women by the end of June. 82 completed. She reports 82% honestly, and does not count women who came to only one session.

panel.heading: Halima reports a missed target
items: Plan: a catch-up session in July

say: She explains the cause in one sentence: two sessions were cancelled after heavy rain flooded the venue.

panel.heading: Halima reports a missed target
items: Plan: a catch-up session in July

say: She gives evidence: the attendance registers and the venue's cancellation message.

panel.heading: Halima reports a missed target
items: Plan: a catch-up session in July

say: And she proposes a catch-up session in July, paid for with unspent venue money.
This builds far more trust than a vague, about 100 women were reached. If you are pressured to inflate a figure, report the true number and raise the concern in writing.

say: Under Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023, personal data must be kept secure. So do not send the whole Data tab, name the women who dropped out, or post sheet links in large groups.

panel.heading: Privacy when you share a report
left: Sheet links in big WhatsApp groups
right: Send the Summary tab or a PDF
Share with named emails, as Viewer

say: Share totals, percentages and codes. Send the Summary or a PDF. Share with named email addresses as Viewer, and set sharing to Restricted, so a forwarded link does not open for strangers.

say: A dashboard is one screen showing 3 to 5 KPIs against their targets. Link every cell with a formula, never type numbers in, so it updates itself. Then add green, amber and red colours with conditional formatting.
For example, Bisi's March sales are 280,000 naira against a 300,000 target. That is 93%, so it shows amber.
Orders are 64 against 60, and conversion is 26% against 25%. Both green.
But repeat customers are 31% against 40%, only 78%. Red.
So her next action is keeping customers, not more advertising. A good dashboard points to the next decision. Keep the percentage visible too, because some readers cannot tell red from green.
To remember. Choose the chart that fits the message, start bars at zero, and let the title say the point.
Give denominators and claim causes carefully. Report missed targets honestly, with a reason and a plan. And keep your dashboard to a few linked KPIs.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Line for trends, bars to compare, table for exact
Start bars at zero; titles state the finding
Report missed targets with reason and plan
Dashboard: 3 to 5 linked KPIs with colours

say: Now practise. Make one honest chart with a title that states the finding. Audit a report against the five-point honesty check, and set your sheet to Restricted. Then build your dashboard with traffic-light colours and one trend.
